subject: What a running Korean Logic actually shows where this product had hand-written Korean
question: The plug-in insert paths and the Library menu item carried Korean literals nobody had checked against a running Logic. What does the application show, and can what it shows be read from Apple's bytes?

reverify.expected: 934 literals: composed_value 15, nibstrings_value 4, nowhere 86, quickhelp_title 170, strings_value 659
reverify.cost: ~40s; reads the app bundle, launches nothing

method: Read a Logic that was already running in Korean with a project open -- nothing was launched. Enumerated the menu bar, the View menu, the window's top-level AXGroups, the control bar's LCD, and every AXGroup and AXButton description in the window by count. Pressed ONE empty audio-FX insert slot to read the insert menu and its format submenu, captured the screen, then pressed Escape twice and re-read the menu bar and window list to confirm the application was unwedged. Then searched the corpus for what had just been read.

canon.used_for: the template Logic composes the Library View-menu item from. `Show Library` is in no corpus in any locale because it is not a string -- it is assembled, and the live menu's `\ub77c\uc774\ube0c\ub7ec\ub9ac \uac00\ub9ac\uae30` is this template's sibling with the Library noun in it
the one step of a plug-in insert path that IS localized. The live format submenu answers `\uc2a4\ud14c\ub808\uc624 | \ub4c0\uc5bc \ubaa8\ub178` while every category above it is English

conclusion:
The plug-in insert menu on a KOREAN Logic answers `Channel EQ | Gain | Compressor | ... | Dynamics | EQ | ... | Utility | Audio Units` -- every category in English, with `최근 사용` the only exception. The occupied slots are AXGroups named `Compressor` and `Channel EQ`, also English. So the four hand-written paths this product carried, half of them built around `유틸리티` and `다이내믹스`, could never have matched: those words are not in that menu. What IS localized is the format submenu, which answers `스테레오 | 듀얼 모노` -- one step, one LabelSet, and the combinatorial explosion that seemed to block ten languages was never there. It also explains why `Utility` is in no corpus: it is plug-in metadata, not Logic's interface text.

The Library menu item is a different shape entirely. `Show Library` is in no corpus in any locale, and neither is the Korean -- because Apple ships `Show %@` and `Hide %@` as TEMPLATES and Logic assembles the item. The live menu reads `라이브러리 가리기`, which the Hide template with the Library noun reproduces exactly, and the Traditional Chinese composes to `顯示「資料庫」` with corner brackets no hand-typed list would have. Only the Show forms belong in the LabelSet: this call site presses what it matches, so carrying the Hide form would CLOSE a panel the caller asked to open.

Composition turned out to be a classifier gap rather than a one-off. Teaching `check-policy-literals-against-canon.py` to reverse-compose a literal against Apple's templates moved `nowhere` from 98 to 86 and explained twelve literals nobody had been able to place -- including `Spuren Titel` and `Spuren enthält`, German track labels this repository had measured live and could not cite.
limits: One locale. Everything here was read from a Korean Logic; that the German insert menu is also English is an inference from the same plug-in metadata being locale-free, not a reading.

The composition check accepts a literal when SOME committed template explains it with a noun the corpus holds in that locale. A 32-bit collision in the absence set can only make an absent noun look present, so the direction it can be wrong in is accepting a composition that is not real -- which leaves a literal explained by the wrong template rather than refusing a true one.

`docs/canon/TEMPLATES.json` holds only the templates an answer rests on. Logic ships 500 single-placeholder templates and all ten locales of each is 278 KB, which is the size this repository already refuses for the row index.
The insert menu was opened once, on one empty slot, and closed with Escape. Whether every strip offers the same categories was not checked.
`showLibraryMenuItem` has no `derivedFrom`: it is two rows multiplied, and `check-labelsets-are-derived.py` verifies one row. Nothing offline checks the composition itself.
